subject: Learning Methods
title: Growth Mindset and Metacognition
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Growth Mindset and Metacognition.

hook.text: Dweck found that students who believed ability is fixed avoided challenges. Those who saw growth embraced them.

buildup.text: A growth mindset sees errors as information. A fixed mindset sees them as proof of inadequacy.

discovery.text: Metacognition requires a growth mindset because self-monitoring means confronting your own ignorance regularly.

twist.text: Growth mindset alone is not enough. You also need the metacognitive skills to translate the belief into action.

climax.text: When you discover a gap, say 'I don't know this yet' instead of 'I can't do this.' The word yet changes everything.

punchline.text: Yet is the most powerful word in learning.

quiz.question: Why does metacognition require a growth mindset?
options: Fixed mindset learners cannot use study strategies
Self-monitoring means regularly confronting your own ignorance
Growth mindset eliminates the need for self-testing
